description: Comprehensive question bank derived from Karnataka Services FDA/SDA Notes (Services Sector, IT/BT, Banking, Tourism, Education, Healthcare, Transport, Trade) and Economic Survey 2025-26. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: The services sector is also known as which sector?
questions.explanation: The services sector is also called the tertiary sector.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: The services sector consists of economic activities that provide:

options.B: Services rather than directly extracting natural resources or manufacturing goods

questions.explanation: The services sector provides services rather than directly extracting natural resources or manufacturing physical goods.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a services-sector activity?
questions.explanation: Iron ore mining is a primary sector activity (extraction of natural resources), not a services-sector activity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a services-sector activity?
questions.explanation: Insurance is a services-sector activity. Agriculture, manufacturing and fishing are primary/secondary sector activities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is the services sector important to Karnataka's economy?

options.A: It is the smallest contributor to the economy
options.B: It is the largest contributor to Karnataka's economy
options.C: It only provides employment in rural areas

questions.explanation: The services sector is the largest contributor to Karnataka's economy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the services sector's share in Karnataka's Gross State Value Added (GSVA) in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The services sector's share in Karnataka's GSVA in 2025-26 was approximately 69.87 per cent at current prices (Advance Estimates, Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the estimated real growth rate of Karnataka's services sector in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The estimated real growth rate of Karnataka's services sector in 2025-26 was 8.1 per cent at constant prices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the real growth rate of Karnataka's services sector in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The services sector grew at 8.4 per cent in 2024-25, compared with 8.1 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: IT-related services were projected to grow by what percentage in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: IT-related services were projected to grow by 10.50 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Hotels and restaurants were projected to grow by what percentage in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Hotels and restaurants were projected to grow by 13.90 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Public administration was projected to grow by what percentage in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Public administration was projected to grow by 8.6 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Other services were projected to grow by what percentage in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Other services were projected to grow by 7.9 per cent in 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between a service-sector share and a service-sector growth rate?

options.B: Share measures proportion of total value added; growth rate measures change in output over time
options.C: Share measures change over time; growth rate measures proportion
options.D: Share is always higher than growth rate

questions.explanation: A sectoral share measures the proportion of total value added contributed by the sector in a given year, whereas a growth rate measures the change in that sector's output over time.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between GSVA and GSDP?

options.A: GSVA includes net product taxes; GSDP does not
options.B: GSVA measures value added by producers; GSDP at market prices includes net product taxes in addition to total gross value added

questions.explanation: GSVA measures value added by producers across sectors, while GSDP at market prices includes net product taxes in addition to the total gross value added.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are knowledge-intensive services?

options.B: Services relying heavily on specialised knowledge, technology, professional skills, research and data
options.C: Services provided only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Knowledge-intensive services rely heavily on specialised knowledge, technology, professional skills, research and data; examples include IT, biotechnology services, finance, consulting, R&D and specialised healthcare.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a knowledge-intensive service?
questions.explanation: Biotechnology services are knowledge-intensive. Retail trade, hospitality and passenger transport are labour-intensive services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are labour-intensive services?

options.A: Services requiring large capital investment only
options.B: Services requiring a relatively large workforce for delivery

questions.explanation: Labour-intensive services require a relatively large workforce for delivery; examples include retail trade, hospitality, personal services, passenger transport and some healthcare and education activities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a labour-intensive service?
questions.explanation: Retail trade is a labour-intensive service. IT consulting, biotechnology research and financial analytics are knowledge-intensive.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major strength of Karnataka's services sector?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru's global technology ecosystem is a major strength of Karnataka's services sector.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major weakness of Karnataka's services sector?

options.A: Concentration of high-value services in Bengaluru

questions.explanation: Concentration of high-value services in Bengaluru is a key challenge/weakness of Karnataka's services sector.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Information Technology (IT)?

options.A: The use of computers, software, networks, databases and digital systems to create, process, store, secure and communicate information
options.B: The manufacturing of computer hardware only
options.C: The extraction of natural resources using machines
options.D: The provision of manual labour services

questions.explanation: IT is the use of computers, software, networks, databases and digital systems to create, process, store, secure and communicate information.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are IT-enabled services (ITeS)?

options.A: Services delivered or supported through information technology
options.B: Services that do not use any technology

questions.explanation: ITeS are services delivered or supported through information technology, such as business-process outsourcing, customer support, data processing, payroll, accounting, remote technical support and back-office operations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between IT and ITeS?

options.A: IT involves development and management of computer systems and software; ITeS uses technology to deliver business and support services
options.C: ITeS involves hardware manufacturing; IT involves services
options.D: IT is only for government; ITeS is only for private sector

questions.explanation: IT mainly involves the development, operation and management of computer systems and software, whereas ITeS uses technology to deliver business and support services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which city is known as the Silicon Valley of India?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is popularly known as the Silicon Valley of India because of its concentration of software companies, start-ups, research institutions, engineering talent and global technology centres.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: According to the Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26, when did Karnataka's IT revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The Survey states that Karnataka's IT revolution began in 1984.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What important IT milestone took place in Bengaluru in 1992?

options.B: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) established its first Earth station
options.D: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission was launched

questions.explanation: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) established its first Earth station in Bengaluru in 1992, supporting the growth of software exports.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Software Technology Parks of India (STPI)?

options.B: An autonomous society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology that supports the software and IT-enabled services industry

questions.explanation: STPI is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology that supports the software and IT-enabled services industry through export facilitation and technology infrastructure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is a Global Capability Centre (GCC)?

options.A: A centre established by a multinational company in another country to perform specialised functions
options.B: A government office for global trade

questions.explanation: A GCC is a centre established by a multinational company in another country to perform specialised functions such as software development, research, analytics, finance, engineering, cybersecurity and business operations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many new GCCs does Karnataka's Global Capability Centres Policy 2024-29 aim to attract?
questions.explanation: The policy aims to attract 500 new GCCs by 2029.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many employment opportunities does Karnataka's GCC Policy 2024-29 aim to generate?
questions.explanation: The policy aims to generate 3.5 lakh employment opportunities by 2029.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the target contribution to Karnataka's economy under the GCC Policy 2024-29?
questions.explanation: The policy aims to contribute USD 50 billion to Karnataka's economy by 2029.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Beyond Bengaluru initiative?

options.A: An initiative to develop technology, innovation and start-up ecosystems in cities outside Bengaluru
options.B: A plan to move all IT companies out of Karnataka

questions.explanation: Beyond Bengaluru is an initiative to develop technology, innovation and start-up ecosystems in cities outside Bengaluru, including Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Kalaburagi and Shivamogga.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which cities are included in the Beyond Bengaluru initiative?

options.A: Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Kalaburagi and Shivamogga
options.B: Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata and Hyderabad
options.C: Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bidar, Raichur and Koppal
options.D: Madikeri, Chikkamagaluru, Hassan, Mandya and Chamarajanagar

questions.explanation: Beyond Bengaluru includes Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Kalaburagi and Shivamogga.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM)?

options.A: A State-supported initiative that promotes Karnataka's digital economy and expands technology clusters beyond Bengaluru

questions.explanation: KDEM is a State-supported initiative that promotes Karnataka's digital economy, expands technology clusters beyond Bengaluru, attracts investment and strengthens industry-academia and start-up ecosystems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the approximate outlay of the Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30 has an approximate outlay of ₹518.27 crore.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many new start-ups does the Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30 aim to foster?
questions.explanation: The policy aims to foster 25,000 new start-ups.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many start-ups outside Bengaluru does the Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30 target?
questions.explanation: The policy includes a target of 10,000 start-ups outside Bengaluru.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major IT-related service export of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Software development is a major IT-related service export of Karnataka. Iron ore, coffee and textiles are merchandise exports.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is biotechnology?

options.A: The application of living organisms, cells, biological systems or biological processes to develop products and technologies
options.C: The study of rocks and minerals
options.D: The production of electricity from coal

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is the application of living organisms, cells, biological systems or biological processes to develop products and technologies for healthcare, agriculture, industry and the environment.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major branch of biotechnology?
questions.explanation: Major branches include medical biotechnology, agricultural biotechnology, industrial biotechnology, environmental biotechnology, bioinformatics, molecular biology, genetic engineering and synthetic biology.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which city is the main biotechnology hub of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is the main biotechnology hub of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Karnataka Biotechnology Policy 2024-29 intended to promote?

options.B: Biotechnology research, bio-manufacturing, innovation, start-ups, skills, investment and commercialisation

questions.explanation: The policy aims to strengthen biotechnology research, bio-manufacturing, innovation, start-ups, skills, investment and commercialisation of biotechnology products.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What employment target is stated under Karnataka's Biotechnology Policy 2024-29?
questions.explanation: The policy aims to create 30,000 high-quality jobs by 2029.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is bio-manufacturing?

options.B: Using biological systems, cells, enzymes or microorganisms to produce useful products

questions.explanation: Bio-manufacturing uses biological systems, cells, enzymes or microorganisms to produce medicines, vaccines, industrial chemicals, materials, food ingredients and other useful products.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is bioinformatics?

options.A: The use of computational tools, statistics and databases to analyse biological data such as DNA, RNA, protein sequences and molecular structures
options.B: The study of human behaviour and society
options.C: The manufacturing of biological products using machines only
options.D: The study of rocks and minerals

questions.explanation: Bioinformatics uses computational tools, statistics and databases to analyse biological data such as DNA, RNA, protein sequences and molecular structures.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following are prominent Bengaluru-based biotechnology and life-science companies?
questions.explanation: Biocon and Syngene International are prominent Bengaluru-based biotechnology and life-science companies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge facing IT/BT services in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Challenges include rapid technological change, global competition, cyber-security risks, specialised skill shortages, R&D costs, regulatory requirements and concentration of high-value activity in Bengaluru.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is banking?

options.A: The business of accepting deposits from the public, safeguarding and transferring money, providing loans and offering payment and other financial services
options.C: The extraction of gold from mines

questions.explanation: Banking is the business of accepting deposits from the public, safeguarding and transferring money, providing loans and offering payment and other financial services under applicable regulation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a main function of commercial banks?
questions.explanation: Commercial banks accept deposits, provide loans and advances, facilitate payments and remittances, create credit, offer digital banking and provide services such as cards, lockers and foreign-exchange transactions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?
questions.explanation: The RBI is India's central bank. It regulates and supervises the banking system, conducts monetary policy, manages currency issuance and supports financial stability and payment systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the RBI?

options.B: Regulating and supervising the banking system

questions.explanation: The RBI does not provide direct loans to farmers; that is the role of institutions like NABARD and cooperative banks. The RBI conducts monetary policy, regulates banks and manages currency issuance.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) in Karnataka?

options.B: A coordination forum between banks, the State Government and other institutions for reviewing banking development, credit flow and financial inclusion

questions.explanation: SLBC is a coordination forum between banks, the State Government and other institutions for reviewing banking development, credit flow, financial inclusion and implementation of banking-related programmes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the role of NABARD?

options.B: Supporting agriculture and rural development through refinance, development programmes and rural credit planning

questions.explanation: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development is an apex development financial institution that supports agriculture and rural development through refinance, development programmes, institutional strengthening and rural credit planning.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is a Regional Rural Bank (RRB)?

options.A: A bank established to provide banking and credit facilities mainly to rural areas
options.B: A bank that operates only in urban areas

questions.explanation: An RRB is a bank established to provide banking and credit facilities mainly to rural areas, especially small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans and small entrepreneurs.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is a cooperative bank?

options.A: A bank owned by the central government
options.B: A financial institution organised on cooperative principles to provide banking and credit services to its members

questions.explanation: A cooperative bank is a financial institution organised on cooperative principles to provide banking and credit services to its members and other eligible customers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is a District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB)?

options.A: A district-level cooperative bank that links State cooperative banks and primary agricultural credit societies

questions.explanation: A DCCB is a district-level cooperative bank that forms an important link in the short-term rural cooperative credit structure between State cooperative banks and primary agricultural credit societies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is a Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS)?

options.A: A village-level cooperative credit institution providing short-term and medium-term credit to farmer members

questions.explanation: A PACS is a village-level cooperative credit institution that provides short-term and medium-term credit and related services to its farmer members.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is financial inclusion?

options.A: Ensuring that individuals and businesses have access to affordable and appropriate banking, credit, insurance, pension and payment services
options.B: Excluding poor people from banking services
options.C: Providing banking services only to rich people
options.D: Providing banking services only in urban areas

questions.explanation: Financial inclusion means ensuring that individuals and businesses, especially low-income and underserved groups, have access to affordable and appropriate banking, credit, insurance, pension and payment services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is priority-sector lending?

options.B: RBI-directed allocation of a specified portion of bank credit to important sectors such as agriculture, micro and small enterprises, education and housing

questions.explanation: Priority-sector lending is the RBI-directed allocation of a specified portion of bank credit to important sectors such as agriculture, micro and small enterprises, education, housing, renewable energy and weaker sections.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: When is a loan generally classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA)?

options.A: When interest or principal remains overdue for more than 30 days
options.B: When interest or principal remains overdue for more than 60 days
options.C: When interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days
options.D: When interest or principal remains overdue for more than 180 days

questions.explanation: A loan or advance is generally classified as a non-performing asset when interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days, subject to RBI rules and applicable exceptions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between a savings account and a current account?

options.A: A savings account is for businesses; a current account is for individuals
options.B: A savings account is mainly for individuals to save money and earn interest; a current account is for frequent transactions by businesses and generally does not pay interest
options.D: A current account pays higher interest than a savings account

questions.explanation: A savings account is mainly intended for individuals to save money and earn interest, while a current account is designed for frequent transactions by businesses and generally does not pay interest.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is digital banking?

options.A: Delivery of banking services through electronic channels such as mobile applications and internet banking
options.B: Banking conducted only through physical branches
options.C: Banking conducted only through post offices

questions.explanation: Digital banking is the delivery of banking services through electronic channels such as mobile applications, internet banking and other digital platforms.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Unified Payments Interface (UPI)?

options.A: An instant payment system developed by NPCI that enables interoperable bank-to-bank transfers through mobile applications

questions.explanation: UPI is an instant payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) that enables interoperable bank-to-bank transfers through mobile applications and supported payment interfaces.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which organisation developed UPI?
questions.explanation: UPI was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). RBI is the central bank and regulator, not the creator of UPI.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between NEFT, RTGS and IMPS?

options.A: NEFT processes in batches at regular intervals; RTGS settles individually in real time for high-value transfers; IMPS provides immediate interbank transfers including outside normal banking hours
options.C: NEFT is for high-value transfers only; RTGS is for small transfers
options.D: IMPS is only for international transfers

questions.explanation: NEFT transfers funds through batches processed at regular intervals; RTGS settles transactions individually in real time and is generally used for high-value transfers; IMPS provides immediate interbank fund transfers, including outside normal banking hours.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many categories of banks were operating in Karnataka according to the Economic Survey 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The Survey lists 12 categories: 12 public-sector banks, 21 private commercial banks, 1 Regional Rural Bank, 1 Apex Cooperative Bank, 21 DCC Banks, 1 KSCARD Bank, 1 KSFC, 8 Small Finance Banks, 3 Payments Banks and 1 Local Area Bank.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many bank branches were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 12,659 bank branches: 4,449 rural, 2,885 semi-urban and 5,325 urban branches, according to the Economic Survey 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many rural bank branches were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 4,449 rural bank branches as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many semi-urban bank branches were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 2,885 semi-urban bank branches as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many urban bank branches were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 5,325 urban bank branches as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many ATMs were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 15,398 ATMs: 1,949 rural, 3,210 semi-urban and 10,239 urban ATMs.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many rural ATMs were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 1,949 rural ATMs as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many semi-urban ATMs were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 3,210 semi-urban ATMs as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many urban ATMs were reported in Karnataka as of September 2025?
questions.explanation: Karnataka had 10,239 urban ATMs as of September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Were there any unbanked villages in Karnataka according to the Economic Survey 2025-26?

options.C: No, there were no unbanked villages reported at the time of reporting

questions.explanation: The Survey reported that there were no unbanked villages in the State at the time of reporting.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which major bank merged with Canara Bank in 2020?
questions.explanation: Syndicate Bank merged with Canara Bank in 2020.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which major bank merged with Bank of Baroda in 2019?
questions.explanation: Vijaya Bank merged with Bank of Baroda in 2019.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following banks has historical origins or important institutional connections with Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Canara Bank, Karnataka Bank, Syndicate Bank and Vijaya Bank have important historical links with Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major banking challenge in Karnataka?

options.A: Uneven access to formal credit for small businesses and farmers

questions.explanation: Challenges include uneven access to formal credit for small businesses and farmers, financial literacy gaps, cyber fraud, non-performing assets, rural service delivery and the need to expand secure digital access.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is tourism?

options.A: Travel and temporary stays outside a person's usual environment for leisure, business, pilgrimage, education, health or other purposes

questions.explanation: Tourism refers to travel and temporary stays outside a person's usual environment for leisure, business, pilgrimage, education, health or other purposes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is tourism important to Karnataka's economy?

options.B: It supports hotels, restaurants, transport and local businesses
options.C: It promotes cultural heritage and infrastructure development

questions.explanation: Tourism generates income and employment, supports hotels, restaurants, transport, handicrafts and local businesses, promotes cultural heritage and encourages infrastructure development.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of tourism in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major types include heritage tourism, religious and pilgrimage tourism, eco-tourism, wildlife tourism, coastal tourism, adventure tourism, rural tourism, medical and wellness tourism, cultural tourism and business tourism.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an important heritage tourism destination in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Hampi, Pattadakal, Badami, Aihole, Mysuru, Srirangapatna, Belur, Halebidu and Vijayapura are important heritage destinations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which UNESCO World Heritage properties are located in Karnataka?

options.C: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura)

questions.explanation: The Group of Monuments at Hampi; the Group of Monuments at Pattadakal; and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura) are UNESCO World Heritage properties in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an important wildlife and eco-tourism destination in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bandipur, Nagarahole, Bannerghatta, Bhadra, Dandeli-Anshi, Kali Tiger Reserve, Kudremukh and the Western Ghats are important wildlife and nature tourism areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an important coastal tourism destination in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Gokarna, Karwar, Murudeshwar, Udupi, Malpe, Maravanthe, Kundapura and Mangaluru are important coastal destinations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an important religious tourism centre in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya, Udupi, Kollur, Sringeri, Nanjangud, Melukote, Chamundeshwari Temple in Mysuru and Yellamma/Savadatti are important pilgrimage centres.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29 aimed at?

options.A: Integrated and sustainable tourism development, investment facilitation, destination improvement and employment generation

questions.explanation: It is the State policy for integrated and sustainable tourism development, investment facilitation, destination improvement, employment generation and wider access to lesser-known tourist destinations.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What investment was envisaged under Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Tourism Vision Group envisaged ₹5,000 crore of investment during the 2024-29 policy period.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many direct and indirect employment opportunities were envisaged under Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29?
questions.explanation: The policy envisaged approximately 10 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities during the 2024-29 policy period.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many domestic tourist visits were recorded in Karnataka in 2024?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported 3,047.08 lakh domestic tourist visits in 2024.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many foreign tourist visits were recorded in Karnataka in 2024?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported 4.85 lakh foreign tourist visits in 2024.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the total number of tourist visits in Karnataka in 2024?
questions.explanation: The total was 3,051.94 lakh visits in 2024 (3,047.08 lakh domestic + 4.85 lakh foreign).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many domestic tourist visits were recorded in Karnataka during 2025 up to December?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported 3,017.47 lakh domestic visits up to December 2025 (partial-year figure).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How many foreign tourist visits were recorded in Karnataka during 2025 up to December?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported 4.37 lakh foreign visits up to December 2025 (partial-year figure).

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the total number of tourist visits in Karnataka during 2025 up to December?
questions.explanation: The total was 3,021.85 lakh visits up to December 2025 (3,017.47 lakh domestic + 4.37 lakh foreign). This is a partial-year figure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the theme of World Tourism Day 2025 as observed in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The theme was 'Tourism & Sustainable Transformation', observed on 27 September 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the special tourism theme for Karnataka in 2025-26?

options.B: Year of Adventure with the theme 'Script Your Adventure'

questions.explanation: The State observed 2025-26 as the Year of Adventure with the theme 'Script Your Adventure'.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is sustainable tourism?

options.A: Tourism that considers present and future economic, social and environmental impacts while meeting the needs of visitors, industry, environment and host communities
options.C: Tourism that only benefits the industry
options.D: Tourism that only benefits foreign visitors

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is retail trade?

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is internal trade?

options.B: The exchange of goods and services across national borders

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

options.B: A good or service purchased from a supplier in another economy

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is an import?

options.B: A good or service sold to a buyer in another economy
